title: Cloudflare and VoidZero Introduce tsrs: An AI-Generated Rust Port of TypeScript
gist: Cloudflare, VoidZero and Owner.com's Max Schwenk released tsrs, an experimental Rust port of the TypeScript compiler written entirely by AI agents led by Claude Opus 5.5 using TypeScript's 15,197 conformance tests as spec, claiming up to 8x faster checking and ~70% less memory than TypeScript 7.0. Independent tests show smaller gains (5.3x vs 7.0, 2.7x vs the 7.1 beta), and Cloudflare is merging it with Theo Browne's rival tsc-rs.

insights.claim: Max Schwenk of Owner.com says he wrote zero code for tsrs, instead directing AI agents led by Claude Opus 5.5 to produce a faithful port of the TypeScript compiler using TypeScript's own 15,197 conformance cases as the specification.
insights.so_what: Shows frontier coding agents can deliver large, spec-backed system rewrites, a strong demand signal for agentic coding.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis

insights.claim: Peter Steinberger contrasted Microsoft needing a team and two years to rewrite the TypeScript compiler in Go with agents producing something significantly better within weeks.
insights.so_what: Suggests AI agents compress the cost and timeline of large software rewrites, threatening incumbent engineering moats.
insights.quote: Kind of amazing that it took Microsoft a team and two years to rewrite the TS compiler in go, and now you can just let an agent rip and get sth significantly better within weeks.
insights.locator: Moved to tsrs over the weekend
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis

insights.claim: Some developers question whether tsrs's arena-based, never-freed memory model is sound.
insights.so_what: AI-generated system code may carry architectural risks that benchmarks miss.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis

insights.claim: Cloudflare claims tsrs delivers up to 8x faster type checking and around 70% less memory than TypeScript 7.0 at the same number of checker workers.
insights.so_what: Headline claims for build-tool speedups are a Cloudflare developer-ecosystem play.
insights.locator: The headline numbers are a claimed
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis

insights.claim: On Owner.com's 37,000-file monolith, a type check that needed 19 GiB and 80 seconds on TypeScript 7.0 dropped to 7 seconds with tsrs.
insights.so_what: Large codebases see order-of-magnitude CI and dev-loop savings.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis

insights.claim: An independent benchmark found 5.3x faster checking and 72% less memory with identical diagnostics, but tsrs exits with code 2 on type errors where tsc exits 1, which could silently break CI scripts.
insights.so_what: Drop-in claims hide compatibility edge cases that slow enterprise adoption.
insights.locator: One developer benchmarked both npm packages
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis

insights.claim: Against the newer TypeScript 7.1 beta, ImportStatic measured only a 2.7x gain, showing the 8x headline relies on an older baseline.
insights.so_what: Vendor benchmark headlines should be discounted against moving baselines.
insights.locator: One developer benchmarked both npm packages
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis

insights.claim: TypeScript's Daniel Rosenwasser argued much of tsrs's speed does not come down to language choice, and optimisations discovered in tsrs are feeding into a leaner TypeScript 7.1.
insights.so_what: Microsoft's Go compiler may close the gap, limiting tsrs's durable advantage.
insights.quote: does not just come down to language choice
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis

insights.claim: Cloudflare stresses tsrs is not a fork, with the TypeScript team retaining full control of language design, and the project is incubated inside VoidZero's Oxc toolchain.
insights.so_what: Cloudflare is building influence over the JavaScript toolchain via VoidZero while avoiding conflict with Microsoft.
insights.locator: tsrs, a Rust port of the TypeScript
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis

insights.claim: Writing the compiler in Rust enables compiling to WebAssembly via @tsrs/wasm so type checks can run in a browser or on Cloudflare Workers without bundling a garbage collector as a Go binary would.
insights.so_what: Ties the tool strategically to Cloudflare's Workers edge platform.
insights.locator: The headline numbers are a claimed
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis

insights.claim: Rather than compete, Cloudflare is merging Theo Browne's rival Rust port tsc-rs with tsrs into a single package, adding language server and content mapper support, alongside Microsoft's Go-based tsgo.
insights.so_what: Consolidation strengthens Cloudflare's position in Rust-based JS tooling.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis

insights.claim: tsrs remains experimental, lacking watch mode and a language server, and tracks TypeScript 7, so teams on TypeScript 5 or 6 must first adopt Microsoft's native Go port.
insights.so_what: Near-term adoption is limited to early adopters already on TypeScript 7.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
